title: Promises After Personal Duplication: one claim, divided responsibility
status: conceptual proposal; not a completed essay
central_question: When one promisor branches into two psychologically continuous successors, what happens to the promisee's claim and who must answer for it?
provisional_claim: Branching alone neither extinguishes one outstanding promised performance nor multiplies it. Qualifying successors may share bounded, alternative responsibility for securing the single performance, discharged once it is completed.

included: Harmless hypothetical branching into two successors
One recipient-directed promise with one specified performance
Successors who retain some continuity with the promissory agency and practical control
excluded_or_conditional: A metaphysical proof that either or both successors are numerically identical to the promisor
Unlimited full liability for each successor
Claims about a real technology or legal system

premises.claim: A promise creates a recipient-directed claim with a specified object and scale.
premises.role: fix the object of the entitlement
premises.support_needed: Primary-source comparison of promise, claim-right and assurance accounts.

premises.claim: Branching alone neither performs the promise nor changes its specified object.
premises.role: rule out automatic cancellation and multiplication
premises.support_needed: Test against promises whose terms make the promisor's unique identity essential.

premises.claim: A successor with responsibility-relevant continuity and meaningful control is a candidate bearer of duties concerning the outstanding claim.
premises.role: connect the persisting claim to future agents without assuming numerical identity
premises.support_needed: Defend the continuity/control threshold; test forced branching and radical divergence.

premises.claim: Successor responsibility must protect the claim without creating a multiplied or unlimited burden.
premises.support_needed: Compare equal shares, joint liability, and bounded alternatives against responsibility theories.

premises.claim: A bounded duty to secure one performance can preserve the original claim while allowing a single discharge and limiting successor burden.
premises.support_needed: Test whether limited coordination is still an unconsented new relationship; specify fair-share metric.

inference: P1 and P2 keep the recipient's single unsatisfied claim in place. P3 identifies qualifying successors as possible duty bearers. P4 excludes automatic per-branch duplication and release. P5 supplies a defeasible allocation model: alternative performance where either can act, task-specific cooperation where necessary, one discharge, and an aggregate burden cap.

qualifying_successor_test: causal/practical continuity with the promissory agency
ability to understand the outstanding claim as arising from that agency
rule_components.discharge: one adequate performance discharges the shared claim; no duplicate object is owed
rule_components.burden: reasonable task-specific means, with total burden no greater than fair fulfillment of the original promise
rule_components.default: least-burden feasible route is provisional; a fair-share formula remains unresolved
rule_components.identity_sensitive_promises: outside default rule when unique identity is part of the promise's point or terms

worked_case.setup: Mara promises Lee one sculpture, branches into A and B, and both remember and can act on the promise.
worked_case.case_one: A holds the work and can finish it at ordinary cost. A's delivery discharges the one claim; B owes no second sculpture.
worked_case.case_two: A holds the work and B has an essential tool. Only reasonable, task-specific assistance within the original burden envelope may be required.
worked_case.stress_case: If the promise was expressly about Mara personally, successor performance may not satisfy it.

objection.claim: Nonconsenting successors may have incompatible lives and no reason to enter a cooperative relationship; calling the burden inherited may disguise a new duty.
objection.proposed_answer: Any duty is addressed to the promisee, derives from the outstanding claim rather than a new relationship between successors, and is limited to steps reasonably necessary for one discharge.
objection.residual_risk: This answer does not establish that a duty can transfer to numerically distinct, nonconsenting successors; if bounded cooperation is still impermissible, narrow to cases where one successor can perform alone or abandon the rule.

assessor_engagement.source: Astra assessment; separately attributed contribution astra-assessment-idea-007
assessor_engagement.challenge: Why does each nonconsenting successor inherit a backup duty, and how is its fair burden fixed?
assessor_engagement.response: Separate succession from blame; require responsibility-relevant continuity and practical control; cap total burden; identify the fair-share formula as unresolved rather than solved.

assessor_engagement.challenge: Can joint responsibility be imposed without creating a new unconsented cooperative relationship?
assessor_engagement.response: Treat the duty as promisee-directed and task-specific, not a general relationship; concede that necessity of cooperation may still defeat the rule.

assessor_engagement.challenge: Do not treat memory as automatic full liability; distinguish assurance preservation from an assumed identity answer.
assessor_engagement.response: Memory is relevant but insufficient; require an agency-continuity and control test and leave metaphysical identity open.

failure_conditions: A defensible account bars transfer of claim-directed duties to distinct nonconsenting successors.
The qualifying-successor test cannot be stated without assuming the identity conclusion.
A bounded duty to coordinate is indistinguishable from the new relationship the objection rejects.
Identity-sensitive, forced-branching, harmful, or nontransferable-performance cases defeat the rule without a principled scope limit.

research_status.closest_alternative: Not established; the identity-only rival in the selected sketch is too narrow to establish the closest literature.
